title: You are God's temple (1 Corinthians 3:10–23)
hookLine: the church, together, is where the Spirit lives
tomorrow: how do you answer an insult the way Paul did?

lines: YE ARE THE TEMPLE OF GOD.
cards: Ask a kid where God lives, and you may hear: up in the sky, or at church. Paul's answer to Corinth is neither: "Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?"
That one small word changes who is in the room. Christians read it in two ways, and both readings can quote Paul.

teach.b: First the build-up. Paul calls himself a masterbuilder who laid the foundation: "For other foundation can no man lay than that is laid, which is Jesus Christ."
What others build on top, gold or straw, will be tested by fire. Then the temple, and the two readings. The first says: look at the grammar.
In the King James, ye is plural, and the Greek here is plural too. Not you alone in your room; all of you, together, quarrels and all. "For the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are."
On this view the holy place is the gathered church, and tearing it into fan clubs is damaging a temple.

teach.h: ONE READING: YE, ALL OF YOU.
teach.b: The second reading says: Paul makes it personal too. Later in this same letter he uses the temple word for one person's body.
On this view each believer carries the temple, and how you treat yourself and others is holy business.

teach.h: ALL ARE YOURS; YE ARE CHRIST'S.
teach.b: Some Christians hear mostly the church in this chapter and the person in the later one; some hear both everywhere.
Paul ends this chapter on the people, not their leaders: "all are yours; And ye are Christ's; and Christ is God's."

how: Christians gather in many kinds of places, from cathedrals to living rooms, and some churches speak of the people, not the building, as the church.

games.q: what does “you are god's temple” mean?
o: the Temple in Jerusalem rebuilt by Herod
Paul's picture of the church as God's dwelling
a church building made holy by a bishop

s: Paul's temple here is the church building in Corinth
ye are the temple: the people, not stone.
in the King James, ye is plural
ye for many, thou for one. the Greek here is plural too.
Paul says the church belongs to its leaders
it runs the other way: all are yours, and ye are Christ's.

games.q: your friend says 'ye are the temple' is only about the church together, never one person. give the best case for the other reading.
o: later in this letter Paul calls one person's body a temple too.
the King James uses ye for just one person.
temples in Corinth were private homes for one family.
games.why: both readings quote Paul: ye together in chapter 3, your body in chapter 6. some Christians keep both.

practice: Bring to mind the next time your group gathers: a rehearsal, a dinner, a service, a practice.
Choose one thing you'll do there to treat the room as holy, like arriving early, greeting the person on the edge, or putting the phone away. Hold that plan for the rest of the sit.

wordCard.voice: You are God's temple. Paul's picture: not a building of stone, but people, where the Spirit of God dwells.

orig.note: Greek: temple, sanctuary. In 1 Corinthians 3:16: ye are the temple of God.

carryVoice: Hold this close: you are the temple, plural, all of you together, quarrels and all. Go well.
